messages.subject: Advice on calculating price elasticities
parts:
Hello,

I have a large data set (daily sales data for 500 products over two years) and am trying to estimate price elasticities and cross-price elasticities. The end goal is to be able to estimate the volume that will be sold of all 500 products if I change the prices of multiple products. I am seeking advice please on how to best do this in INLA.

I would like to incorporate as much as possible of (1) the own-price elasticity for each product should be fairly similar (same types of product), (2) the products would all have a similar non-linear trend component, and (3) the cross-price elasticities should insignificant for almost all products (it's unreasonable to expect every product affects every other product). 

If I weren't seeking to include cross-price elasticities, (1) and (2) are easy: I would create a random interaction effect between ProductID and price and simply add a non-linear term to the poisson model. The cross-price elasticities present a problem since there are so many coefficients (500 x 499 = ~250K) and material values are sparse. Even setting aside the number of coefficients, since I am fairly confident all of these products are substitutes I am fairly confident the coefficients are >= 0 and a normal prior might not be reasonable. Ideally I'd use something like a pc.prior, but my sense is that wouldn't be possible at this scale. I'd be okay with using a normal prior if necessary.

One last thought: I can use the units sold of the other products rather than the prices if it would be easier (i.e., I don't actually care about cross-price elasticities, I just need to understand how changing prices impacts other products).

Any thoughts would be very much appreciated. Thank you!

messages.author: 0bcf10e0a8f767a2
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Advice on calculating price elasticities
parts:
Thank you Håvard.

Without cross-elasticities, I would do model = inla(Quantity ~ ProductName + f(DaysPassed, model = 'iid') + f(Trend, model = 'rw2') + logPrice + f(ProductID, logPrice, model = 'iid'), family = 'poisson', data = inlaData). Is there a way to incorporate for each ProductName the volumes or prices of all other 499 products, have the relationship be unique between each combination (e.g., a price increase of 1% on product A increases volume of product B by 2% and product C by 3%), constrain the sign (on prices would be >=0 or on volumes would be <=0), and make the prior skewed so values near zero are more likely? If I can't get all of these requests, how can I get the maximum number? Thanks again!
